brief: Citi's rates team says Treasury's Nov 4 refunding dealer questionnaire, published Friday, confirms its prior view that Treasury will cut 20Y and 30Y auction sizes by $3bn each, taking 20Y new issues to $13bn and 30Y to $22bn. Citi reads the buyback question as proof the long-end buyback cap increase was about capping yields, not market functioning: 30Y auctions stopped through WI by -0.23bp over the past year, the first two $6bn-cap buyback operations went unmaxed, but the next three were oversubscribed. Despite the buybacks, 30Y yields are over 20bps higher than when the cap increase was announced and 60bps higher year-to-date. The second question, on structural demand changes and future auction sizes, leads Citi to tie the cut to long-end demand being partly cannibalized by hyperscaler bond issuance. Citi expects the lost long-end supply to shift into bills, projecting bills reaching 24.4% of marketable debt by end-2027, with a debt-ceiling bind forcing a TGA drawdown by Q2 2027. Citi stays tactically neutral on duration, receiving October OIS and expecting a Fed pause in October followed by a December hike. Goldman Prime reports hedge funds have net sold AI stocks for five straight sessions, reversing all 2025's net buying.
